[[0]] Apple TV 剛剛取得《Dustfall》嘅全球串流播映權。《Dustfall》係一套來自澳洲嘅犯罪劇集，亦係呢個串流平台近期第二次偏離原先「只播自家製節目」嘅策略。

[[1]] Apple has started acquiring more television series, no longer sticking to an 'all original' strategy

[[2]] Since its launch in 2019, Apple TV has refused to follow the traditional streaming platform approach of acquiring pre-existing content, instead prioritising original productions.

[[3]] Apple has remained very consistent with its 'originals only' strategy. Until recently, the only exceptions were children's content tied to its original programming (such as Peanuts holiday specials), and limited-run affiliated films.

[[4]] However, that changed this week when the widely acclaimed comedy Small Prophets premiered on Apple, following the tech giant's acquisition of the hit British series over the summer.

[[5]] Small Prophets appears to be a shrewd acquisition. Early reviews have hailed it as a 'masterpiece' and possibly 'the best show on Apple this year'.

[[6]] Today, Apple announced its second acquisition. The Australian crime drama starring Anna Torv, Dustfall, will join the streaming platform in 2027.

[[7]] Like Small Prophets, Dustfall is produced by an international production company and will premiere in select overseas territories before debuting globally on Apple TV.

[[8]] It's clear that Apple's stance on acquiring content is no longer what it once was.

[[9]] While the streaming platform hasn't abandoned its effective 'originals-first' approach, bringing in high-quality series from around the world to enrich its library does represent a strategic shift.

[[10]] This shift has me excited to see whether it will accelerate going forward.

[[11]] What do you think about Apple TV acquiring third-party series? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.

[[12]] Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, or it can be subscribed to via the Apple One bundle.
